titleStmt.title: Shiji 史记 · 秦庄襄王二年: notes

div.interp: The second year of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, 248 BC; the king is the subject.
定太原: the Tables and the Hereditary Houses (§2, §3) give the campaign as the taking of Yuci and thirty-seven cities, and the Hereditary House of Yan adds that Qin set up Taiyuan Commandery.
蒙驚: the three-commentary edition reads 蒙驁, Meng Ao, as the Basic Annals (§1).

The Zhengyi on the Basic Annals (案：取三十七城，并、代、朔三州之地矣): the thirty-seven Fortresses are the lands of the three States of Bingzhou, Daizhou and Shuozhou, in the names of the Tang; the Hereditary Houses (§3) count them as taken at Yuci.
日蝕: entered in the Table's Qin column for the year.
徙封於吳: from the twelve Counties north of the Huai to the old seat of Wu, as the Biography of Lord Chunshen (§4) tells.
The seventh year of King Xi of Yan, 248 BC.
榆次三十七城: the thirty-seven Fortresses of the Table's entry (§2), Yuci the first of them.
大原 is written for 太原. The Basic Annals of Qin put the founding of Taiyuan Commandery in the next year, the king's third.
The eighteenth year of King Xiaocheng of Zhao, 248 BC.
Lian Po, Acting Chancellor of State since the fifteenth year (251 BC) in this Hereditary House, here Chancellor of State.
262 BC. The passage is the one already given in the Biography for 255 BC (§4), repeated here for the move it dates.
The fifteenth year of King Kaolie, 248 BC, where the Table (§2) enters the move of the fief to Wu.
The second year of King Zhuangxiang of Qin, 248 BC; the Biography continues the sentence begun under the first year (249 BC, §5).

The chapter is the one appended under 256 BC (§6), where its translation and notes first appear; it is repeated here as the compiler adduces it for Jing Ji's campaign. The two graphs the manuscript leaves illegible are given as 〓, as there.
In the appended chapter the characters in parentheses are the editors' readings of the manuscript graphs before them (粱 read 梁, 侍 read 待, and so on); the translation follows the readings.
割挚马免: no published reading of the phrase was found; 挚 is taken as 贽, "gifts", and the rendering is approximate.
股符〓去壁: 〓 marks a graph illegible in the manuscript. The Wikisource transcription of the text reads 股符胠壁, 胠 "to break open" and 壁 "rampart"; 股 is unexplained, and the rendering is tentative.
文信侯: Lü Buwei, under the title the Zhanguo zonghengjia shu gives him.
王〓: the graph after 王 is illegible in the manuscript.
赍赵 (齎趙 in the transcription): 齎 is probably a loan for 挤, "to press"; the reading is not settled.
